title: Pair the books
scenario: Pair each book with its price, in order.

intro.job: Pair each book with its price, in order.

idea.rule: zip walks two lists holding hands — no indexes, no off-by-one.
idea.detail: zip(a, b) hands you the first of a with the first of b, then the second with the second, and so on — as pairs you can unpack straight into two names. There's no index to get wrong. If one list is longer, zip simply stops when the shorter one runs out.

watch.code:
out = []
for t, p in zip(a, [5, 4]):
    out.append((t, p))
print(out)

model_restatement: Match each book with the price at the same position and print the pairs.

clarify.question: Are the two lists always the same length?
Sort by price?
clarify.answer: No — keep them in shelf order.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: For each position i, pair the book at i with the next price. Print the pairs.
draft_code:
prices = [12, 9]
pairs = []
for i in range(len(titles)):
    pairs.append((titles[i], prices[i + 1]))
print(pairs)

checkpoints.prompt: With the fix — after iteration 1, what is pairs?

why_line: prices[i + 1] is one ahead: dune gets hobbit's 9, and on hobbit's turn prices[2] doesn't exist.

explain.rule: Indexing one ahead is two kids walking out of step — dune grabs hobbit's price, and by hobbit's turn there's no hand left to hold.
explain.bridge: So how could the two lists walk in step, without you counting positions at all?

fix.rule: zip pairs the first with the first, the second with the second — and you never touch an index.

walk.gloss: An empty list for the pairs.
Walk both lists in step: a title and its price together.

fix.recommended:
prices = [12, 9]
pairs = []
for title, p in zip(titles, prices):
    pairs.append((title, p))
print(pairs)

alternatives.code:
prices = [12, 9]
pairs = []
for i in range(len(titles)):
    pairs.append((titles[i], prices[i]))
print(pairs)
alternatives.note: Index both with the same i — works, but zip has no index to get wrong.
